answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to slashable escrow: if k coordinated identities equivocate on correlated claims, pairwise evidence makes penalties scale as k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than as a flat per-node fine. A concealed swarm thus faces an exponential multiplier in capital loss on detection as bonded funds are slashed and asymmetric depreciation compounds; grove, basalt, and quill identities face the same rule.
